behavior_items: The reproducer declares a class template `CW<T>` with a dependent alias `using V = typename decltype(T())::type;`. This forces the compiler to form a dependent `decltype(T())` expression and then refer to its nested member type `::type`.
Because `T` is a template parameter, `T()` is type-dependent. Therefore `decltype(T())::type` is also dependent and cannot be fully resolved during the initial parse of the class template definition.
The class then declares `static void operator=(int) requires requires(V x) { x; } {}`. This is intentionally ill-formed because an assignment operator must be a non-static member function.

The `requires requires(V x) { x; }` portion exercises parsing and pretty-printing of a nested requires-expression attached as a function constraint. The local parameter `V x` refers back to the dependent alias, so the constraint contains dependent type syntax.
GCC is expected to diagnose the declaration regardless of whether the constraint is satisfiable, because the core semantic error is that `operator=` cannot be declared `static`.

To produce that diagnostic, GCC formats the full function declaration/signature for the error message. While printing the constrained declaration, it also tries to pretty-print the nested requires-expression and the dependent type used in `V`.

The bug is not a miscompilation of the template semantics but a diagnostic pretty-printer failure: GCC emits the internal text `decltype_type' not supported by pp_cxx_unqualified_id` inside the error message instead of rendering the source-level type correctly.

That internal fragment indicates the pretty-printer path handling a C++ unqualified-id cannot represent the AST node corresponding to the dependent `decltype(...)`-based type when it appears in this diagnostic context.

The malformed text appears specifically inside the printed requires-clause, showing that the problematic code path is triggered when pretty-printing a constrained member declaration whose constraint mentions a dependent alias expanding to `typename decltype(T())::type`.

So the reproducer exercises three interacting language features at once: dependent `decltype`, a type alias naming a nested dependent type, and a nested requires-expression on a special member operator declaration. The semantic error is ordinary, but the diagnostic rendering for the declaration is broken.

The report notes that the issue reproduces back to early GCC Concepts implementations, suggesting a long-standing diagnostic/pretty-printing bug rather than a recent regression in template or constraint semantics.

gcc/cp/decl.cc.summary: We're initializing a local variable which has a cleanup GUARD. If there are any temporaries used in the initializer INIT of this variable, we need to wrap their cleanups with TRY_CATCH_EXPR (, GUARD) so that the variable will be cleaned up properly if one of them throws. Unfortunately, there's no way to express this properly in terms of nesting, as the regions for the temporaries overlap the region for the variable itself; if there are two temporaries, the variable needs to be the first thing destroyed if either of the temporary destructors throws. However, we only want to run the variable's cleanup if it actually got constructed. So we need to guard the temporary cleanups with the variable's cleanup if they are run on the normal path, but not if they are run on the exceptional path. We implement this by telling honor_protect_cleanup_actions to strip the variable cleanup from the exceptional path. Another approach could be to make the variable cleanup region enclose initialization, but depend on a flag to indicate that the variable is initialized; that's effectively what we do for arrays. But the current approach works fine for non-arrays, and has no code overhead in the usual case
